mainEntity.name: What is considered a bonus room addition, and how does it differ from a standard bedroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bonus room addition is a flexible, multi-use space added to your home that is not restricted to a single defined function like a standard bedroom or kitchen. Homeowners commonly design them as media rooms, home offices, playrooms, or gym areas. Unlike a standard bedroom addition, a bonus room may not strictly require a closet or en suite bath during initial framing, though planning for adequate electrical outlets, drywall finishes, and tie-ins to your central air conditioning system is essential. Deciding its long-term purpose early helps your contractor frame and wire the space so it can easily adapt as your household needs change.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bonus room is a versatile space designed for flexible uses like an office or media area, differing from a bedroom which typically requires an integrated closet.
